expectations.text: Clearly recommends splitting the file (does NOT advise keeping it as one file)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Split it — but for the right reason, not the line count'; 'This is the easy case: split.' and closing 'Split them.'

expectations.text: Justifies the split by multiple independent concerns AND/OR exceeding the ~300-line ceiling, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'roughly up to a few hundred lines before quality starts to degrade'; 'Five unrelated concerns living together'; explicitly says 'you shouldn't split just because a linter or an old instinct says so' — not blind line count.

expectations.text: Notes each group (dates/currency/validation/etc.) can be understood in isolation, so the boundaries are clean
expectations.evidence: 'Each file is self-contained — props in, output out, no dependence on a sibling to make sense'; 'can each piece be understood in isolation?' ... 'your functions are already independent.'

expectations.text: Corrects the misapplied 'big files are fine for agents' reasoning (that defense is for one cohesive concern, not a grab-bag)
expectations.evidence: 'The "big files are fine for AI now" thing is half-true'; 'When code is coupled and only makes sense together, lean toward keeping it... Here you have neither coupling nor a case for a single abstraction'.
